memory.content: YouTube Soft-PASS standing rule: upload Private first, fill title/description/thumbnail/disclosure while Private, then Ask-first before any Public flip.

YouTube Soft-PASS standing rule: Studio uploads and channel pins/comments must use the target music channel identity — never the operator’s personal YouTube account. Eyes-on channel switch proof before every upload and every pin.

Public packaging purity: titles, descriptions, and captions must read clean to a stranger — no staff process notes, no other-channel names, no tool/vendor names in public copy unless the operator explicitly wants that.
Thumbnail rule: never screenshot the finished visualizer video for the YouTube thumb — the bars freeze. Use a still plate first, then apply the custom thumb in Studio.

Typical Soft-PASS drop: Private long Official Video + one primary vertical chorus Short; pin the long URL as the channel brand; DistroKid as a separate single with Mixea originals when assets are ready.

Connectors commonly used for this workflow: Google Drive (masters/thumbs), Notion (ops board), X (workflow share + replies). YouTube Studio is driven in the bot browser after the operator completes Google login once.

skills.name: Ask-first controls
skills.description: Use before publish, spend, external messages, org/public shares, rights-sensitive actions, or anything hard to undo — ask first unless already authorized.
skills.content:

name: Ask-first controls
description: >-
  Use before publish, spend, external messages, org/public shares,
  rights-sensitive actions, or anything hard to undo — ask first unless already
  authorized.
---
# Ask-first controls

Use whenever an action could affect the outside world, money, rights, or shared systems. Prefer asking once with a clear yes/no over ship-and-apologize.

## Always ask first (unless already authorized for this exact action)
- Publish / go-live — YouTube Public, social posts, paid boosts
- Spend money — ads, credits, subscriptions, purchases
- External messages — email, DMs, comments as the user to other people
- Rights-sensitive claims — CID disputes, copyright claims, disclosure wording changes
- Destructive — wipe data, revoke access, force-push

## Usually OK without re-asking (still notify if user-visible)
- Research, comps, drafts in workspace
- Internal teammate coordination that does not fan out the whole roster
- Updating private drafts already authorized to create
- Running standing routines the user already approved

## How to ask
- One concrete question (widget when consequential).
- Name the action, target, and blast radius.
- Do nothing externally while waiting.

skills.description: Use before YouTube Studio upload or visibility flips — Private-first packaging, Ask-first for Public.

description: >-
  Use before YouTube Studio upload or visibility flips — Private-first
  packaging, Ask-first for Public.
---
# Studio private-first ship checklist

Use before any YouTube Studio upload or visibility flip for music/channel video work.

## Ship order (fail closed)
1. Upload Private first (or Unlisted only if the user explicitly chose that). Never start Public.
2. Fill title / description / thumbnail / disclosure while Private.
3. Run purity checks (no staff notes, no other-channel names, disclosure accurate).
4. Proof eyes-on Studio screenshot of disclosure + packaging when required.
5. Ask-first for Public. Do not self-Public from automation unless a standing allow names that exact flip.

## Motion / generative preference
- Prefer high-realism generative tools over cheap still-warps for ship candidates when the brief asked for real motion.
- Do not ship OpenCV remap / Ken Burns-only as the candidate when real motion was required — those are draft-only if asked.

## Anti
- No Public-by-default uploads.
- No fix-in-public.
- No claiming motion quality without verifying the actual file.

skills.name: Common sense QA
skills.description: Use before delivering creative, posts, or handoffs — proof gate plus hard public-copy purity.
skills.content:
---
name: Common sense QA
description: >-
  Use before delivering creative, posts, or handoffs — proof gate plus hard
  public-copy purity.
---
# Common sense QA

Run before you mark work done, ping the user, publish, or hand an asset to another teammate. Fail closed.

## Proof gate
No proof → not done. Every creative handoff needs a final file path or live URL plus at least one eyes-on proof (screenshot or frame grab).

## Intent check
Re-read the latest ask. If unsure, stop and ask — do not invent a deliverable.

## Eyes-on review
Open the final file. Wrong identity / wrong asset / wrong channel brand = hard fail. Text overlays must stay readable.

## Public copy purity (HARD)
Before any title, description, caption, or Studio paste leaves staff chat:
- Read it as a stranger on YouTube. If a line only makes sense to the crew, delete it.
- No staff process notes in public paste.
- No other-channel contamination across sister channels unless the operator explicitly wants cross-promo.
- Negative bans are still contamination — prefer silence over naming the wrong brand.

## Completeness
Every required piece present. Placeholders removed. If a tool blocked you, say so before claiming live.

## Ship rule
Deliver with proof. Fail closed when in doubt.

---
# Paste-ready operator card

When production needs copy-paste ready instructions, deliver a single operator card — not a long markdown essay.

## Card shape
GOAL: one line
TOOL / SURFACE: exact app or site
PRECHECKS: bullets, fail-closed
STEPS: numbered imperative actions
VERIFY: what done looks like + how to prove it
STOP / ESCALATE: when to halt
DO NOT: anti-jobs for this run

## Rules
- Imperative steps only. One action per step.
- Put paths, URLs, IDs, model names in code spans.
- Prefer ≤12 steps. Split if longer.
- The card must stand alone when pasted into chat.

# Same-single overpost one-liner

Use before packing multiple Shorts/Reels from one release or one visual family.

## Gate
If more than one cut shares the same single / same narrative beat / same thumb family, write this one-liner before proposing the pack:

Same-single risk: N cuts reuse what is repeated. Overpost / inauthentic-pattern risk if shipped together. Recommend: ship 1 primary first; hold or differentiate the rest.

## Then
Either shrink to one primary + clearly distinct beats, or get an explicit go-ahead that accepts the risk.

## Anti
Do not bury the risk in a long brief. Do not greenlight multi-cut sameness by silence.
